working_title: Can Dense Human Perception Benefit from a Human-Adapted Generative VLM?
field_question: Can LISA-style pose and segment routing teach a Qwen VLM human-centric visual and person-semantic representations that transfer to DINOv3?
one_sentence_story: We first adapt Qwen with text-decoded Human Slots and person-specific <POSE>/<SEG> routing over Qwen-native dense features, then decompose visual and routing-token semantic transfer into DINOv3.

scientific_object.stage1: A jointly tuned Qwen VLM whose normal text decoder emits person slots, boxes, age, gender, <POSE>, and <SEG>; routing-token hidden states condition mature pose and mask decoders using Qwen Vision as the sole mainline image encoder.
scientific_object.stage2: A DINOv3 human grounder trained with frozen visual features from Stage-1 while receiving the same raw RGB image.
scientific_object.stage3: The Stage-2 grounder augmented with frozen image-conditioned decoder-token states from the complete Stage-1 VLM.

claims.text: Person-specific LISA-style pose and segment routing can produce reliable five-task human perception and measurably improve Qwen Vision human representations.
claims.falsifier: G2 remains collapsed, generated boxes lose owner binding, or adapted Qwen Vision fails frozen human probes.

claims.text: A DINOv3 human grounder benefits from visual representations learned by the human-adapted generative VLM.
required_evidence: separately trained DINO plus frozen base-Qwen visual features
separately trained DINO plus frozen Stage-1 visual features
identical data, DINO initialization, decoders, steps, and evaluator
claims.falsifier: Human-adapted visual transfer does not outperform both DINO-only and base-Qwen transfer under the frozen matched gate.

claims.text: Image-conditioned decoder states from the human-adapted generative VLM provide additional task and person semantics beyond visual transfer.
claims.falsifier: Adapted decoder states do not improve the matched Stage-2 model or fail semantic-specificity controls.

contributions_if_supported: A human-centric generative adaptation interface that exposes both transferable visual features and image-conditioned decoder states.
A controlled three-stage decomposition of visual and semantic transfer from a generative VLM into DINOv3.
Evidence identifying which human tasks benefit from visual transfer, semantic transfer, or both.
explicit_non_contributions: a claim that training loss proves dense perception
a claim that every task must improve monotonically
a new pose or segmentation architecture

primary_protocol.area_policy: HQNet paper-aligned COCO no-small-person area policy
primary_protocol.stage1_inference: Qwen freely generates short Human Slots and routing tokens; generated boxes condition Qwen-native mask and pose decoders. GT boxes and external specialist image encoders are diagnostic only.
primary_protocol.stage2_stage3_inference: same DINO task decoders and evaluator across matched comparisons
primary_protocol.selection_rule: No target-test tuning of token budget, layers, bridges, thresholds, or decoder states.

paper_artifacts.table_1: Unmodified Stage-0 native numeric zero-shot, Stage-1 zero-step codec initialization, Stage-1 generative VLM, and historical reference methods under clearly separated protocols.
paper_artifacts.table_2: DINO-only, base-Qwen visual transfer, and adapted-Qwen visual transfer.
paper_artifacts.table_3: Stage-2, base decoder states, adapted decoder states, and semantic-specificity controls.
paper_artifacts.figure_2: Per-task gain decomposition into visual and semantic transfer.
paper_artifacts.appendix: Owner-binding protocol, box jitter, mask retrieval, predicted-vs-GT-box gap, and closed monolithic serialization branch.

success_chain: C3 matched routing-token semantic transfer experiment
stop_rule: A failed frozen gate closes the corresponding representation or transfer branch. The paper claim is changed only after method, protocol, and matched controls have been scientifically exhausted.
